title: The factory pack: a plugin marketplace built from factory/src and the server policy

story.as_a: machine in the fleet, or a future cloud session
story.i_want_to: install the factory's hooks, skills, scripts and delivery-loop prose as one versioned plugin pack published from the loopctl repo
story.so_that: a factory rule changes in one commit here and reaches every session as a pack version, with no hand-copied file in claude-config

rationale: PRD R10, the bridge: loopctl publishes a factory pack (its hooks, skills and generated policy prose) and claude-config installs it like any plugin. Today the factory's hooks are wired into each machine's settings.json by claude-config's merge-settings.py from settings.shared.json, and loopctl's own orchestration skills are hand copies (skills/loopctl-plan.md here, skills/loopctl-plan/SKILL.md there). After US-52.50 and US-52.51 the sources and the rule values live here; this story generates the installable pack from them and refuses a pack that has drifted from its sources.

acceptance_criteria.description: mix factory.pack writes factory/pack/ as a Claude Code plugin named loopctl-factory: .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/ and hooks/lib/, bin/, skills/, commands/, agents/ and prose/, copied or rendered from factory/src; its hooks/hooks.json registers each pack hook on the same event and matcher claude-config's settings.shared.json gives it today, with commands written as ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/<file>.

factory/pack/policy.json holds Policy.get/0's schema, version and rules (the policy compiled into the pack); hooks/lib/policy.sh policy_get <dotted.path> prints a value from the policy AC-52.52.3 resolves and exits 3 on an unknown path, and every pack hook takes each rule value through policy_get.

policy.sh resolves the policy without ever blocking a session on the network: when ~/.claude/factory-cache/policy.json is missing or older than 300 s, it fetches GET /api/v1/factory/policy through hooks/lib/loopctl.sh with If-None-Match set to the cached version, passing loopctl.sh's per-call timeout argument as 2 s total (loopctl.sh keeps 3 s connect, 5 s total for callers that pass none); a 200 creates the ~/.claude/factory-cache/ directory on first write, outside the versioned plugin root that ~/.claude/factory links to, and replaces the cache atomically (temp file, then mv) with the body and its version, and a 304 refreshes the cache's mtime. When the fetch fails, times out, answers anything else, or returns a schema the pack does not accept (its own and the previous one, PRD R7), it uses the cache; with no cache, or a cached schema the pack does not accept, it uses the pack's own policy.json. It never answers a default that allows everything, and policy_source prints which of fetched, cache or pack was used.

prose/delivery-loop.md is rendered from factory/src/prose/delivery-loop.md.eex with values from the policy: rendering with a fixture policy whose review_rounds.code.ceiling is 5 yields prose that states a ceiling of 5 and never 3.

release/manifest.toml gains [components.factory_pack] with version, minimum and source factory/src/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (the pack's version source, which mix factory.pack copies into factory/pack), and Loopctl.ReleaseSet and mix loopctl.release_set --check and --bump cover it as they cover every other component (AC-52.7.2 to AC-52.7.4); its first minimum equals its version. The built plugin.json's version equals that factory pack version; mix factory.pack exits 1 naming both values when they differ.

mix factory.pack --check exits 1, naming each differing path, when any committed file under factory/pack differs from a fresh build; the CI lint job runs it, so a source or policy edit without a rebuilt pack fails CI.

The repo root carries .claude-plugin/marketplace.json naming the marketplace loopctl-factory with three plugins: loopctl-factory at ./factory/pack, review-round-counter at ./factory/pack-review-rounds, which mix factory.pack builds from the counter source US-52.50 imported (US-52.53 later rewrites that source and depends on this story), and kb-first at ./factory/pack-kb-first, built from the imported plugins/kb-first under its own name so its tool stays mcp__kb-first__kb_followthrough; all at the pack version. The loopctl-factory plugin carries no .mcp.json: it ships bin/loopctl-mcp.sh, the launcher of the user-scope loopctl MCP server, whose default package is rendered as loopctl-mcp-server@<the manifest's MCP package version>, never @latest.

factory/pack/bin/install-link.sh makes ~/.claude/factory a symlink to the installed loopctl-factory plugin root; a second run with the link already correct changes nothing and exits 0, and a missing plugin root exits 4 without touching an existing link.

technical_notes: Why a plugin and not merge-settings.py: /home/mkreyman/workspace/claude-config/bin/merge-settings.py REPLACES the hooks block on each machine from settings.shared.json (:2, its $comment), so a factory hook can only reach a machine through a claude-config commit; plugins are already the fleet's packaging (settings.shared.json:34-53 registers the directory marketplace mkreyman-plugins and enables review-round-counter there, plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json). A plugin pack keeps that installer and moves the source here.

Hook wiring to copy (event and matcher, from /home/mkreyman/workspace/claude-config/settings.shared.json): gate-pr-body.sh :153, block-loop-mode-merge.sh :203, gate-epic-merge-green-base.sh :198, block-catchup-merge.sh :211 (PreToolUse Bash); brief-dispatch.py :289; inject-review-context.sh :331 (PreToolUse Skill); gate-ask-user-question.sh :323 (PreToolUse AskUserQuestion); kb-recall-on-prompt.sh :499 (SubagentStart) and :511 (UserPromptSubmit); block-manual-precommit.sh :395; require-gate-lock.sh :404; inject-fix-contract.sh :446 (PostToolUse); gate-stated-intent.sh :590, gate-unmerged-pr.sh :594, keep-orchestrator-working.sh :598 (Stop). The build never reads claude-config: the wiring is written once, from these lines, into factory/src/hooks/wiring.toml.

The session's inbox read at SessionStart (release 4's replacement of hooks/session-start.sh:406-703, README names table: messaging MCP tools) is a pack hook too: factory/src/hooks/session-inbox.sh, a thin call to the inbox route.

hooks/lib/loopctl.sh is the pack's one HTTP helper for thin calls: key from LOOPCTL_AGENT_KEY (the holder credential, README names table), a 3 s connect and 5 s total timeout by default and an optional per-call total timeout argument a caller may pass (policy.sh passes 2 s, AC-52.52.3), the witness headers loopctl's authenticated routes require (X-Loopctl-STH-Bootstrap then X-Loopctl-Last-Known-STH, as chg's outbox sends them: /home/mkreyman/workspace/chg/cli/src/outbox.rs, commit 5c843a1), and exit 75 on any transport failure so callers fail open.

Values the hooks read today that become policy_get calls: gate-epic-merge-green-base.sh:141 (NEW_TIP_SECONDS), gate-pr-body.sh's section list via bin/pr-body-sections.sh. An environment override that exists today (EPIC_MERGE_NEW_TIP_SECONDS) keeps working for a canary and is not a second source: policy_get answers the env value only when FACTORY_POLICY_OVERRIDE=1, which only canaries set.

Version: this story adds the factory_pack component to release/manifest.toml (AC-52.52.5; US-52.7 created the manifest without it, README names table: release manifest); mix factory.pack reads the manifest's version and never writes it. lib/mix/tasks/factory.pack.ex and lib/loopctl/factory/pack.ex.

~/.claude/factory is the stable path the rendered prose and claude-config's CLAUDE.md import name (US-52.50 rewrote bin paths to ~/.claude/factory/bin/); the plugin cache path carries the version, so a link is needed.
CI: add 'mix factory.pack --check' to the lint job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:134).

Why the MCP server is not a plugin .mcp.json: Claude Code names a plugin's MCP tools mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool> (the fleet's playwright plugin answers as mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_navigate), so a pack-provided server would rename every tool to mcp__plugin_loopctl-factory_loopctl__*. claude-config names mcp__loopctl__* in settings.shared.json's allowlist, in hook matchers and bodies (gate-ask-user-question.sh, kb-recall-on-prompt.sh, session-start.sh and many more hooks and canaries), in the tools lists of every agent under agents/, and in skills and commands; a renamed tool silently drops out of an agent's tool list. So the server stays registered at user scope under the name loopctl (today ~/.claude.json mcpServers.loopctl runs claude-config's bin/loopctl-mcp.sh), and the pack owns its launcher and version instead; US-52.54 repoints the entry. Function-hook plugin tools keep the plugin name (mcp__kb-first__kb_followthrough today, from the mkreyman-plugins marketplace), so kb-first moves without a rename.
non_goals: The review-round counter's thin-call rewrite: US-52.53 (this story only publishes its plugin directory).
Installing the pack on the fleet and deleting the claude-config copies: US-52.54.
Fetching the pack from a private repo with a token: release 11 (README releases table).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.52.3: a session cut off from loopctl enforces the last policy it fetched (the cache), or the policy compiled into its installed pack when it has none, never an allow-all default.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.52.6: the pack is a pure function of factory/src, factory/policy.toml and the manifest, committed and checked in CI, so no machine holds a pack that differs from a commit.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.52.8: install-link.sh changes nothing when the link is already right, so a re-run of the install is safe; mix factory.pack rebuilds the same bytes from the same inputs.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.52.3: the policy fetch runs at most once per 300 s under a 2 s total timeout, and a slow answer takes the cache, so a hook waits at most 2 s on the network; other thin calls keep hooks/lib/loopctl.sh's own timeouts (technical_notes).
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.52.7: the pack is reached through one marketplace at the repo root, installed by Claude Code's plugin installer on each machine.

defaults: Marketplace and plugin name: loopctl-factory; the review counter stays a separate plugin named review-round-counter so its function-hook module and the shell hooks install independently.
Thin-call timeouts: 3 s connect, 5 s total, unless the caller passes loopctl.sh's per-call timeout.

The loopctl MCP server stays a user-scope registration named loopctl, launched by the pack's bin/loopctl-mcp.sh at the release-set version, not a plugin .mcp.json, so every mcp__loopctl__* name keeps working (owner may change; a plugin server would rename the tools, technical_notes).
Policy fetch: 2 s total timeout, at most once per 300 s; cache at ~/.claude/factory-cache/policy.json (owner may change).
definition_of_done: mix factory.pack --check exits 0 on the epic branch, and claude plugin validate . passes.
On one fleet machine: claude plugin marketplace add pointing at the epic branch, then claude plugin install loopctl-factory@loopctl-factory, lists the pack's skills and hooks in a new session.
